text:
Anthony Duclair has worn nine NHL sweaters, and on Long Island he's playing a useful part on a Long Island team that has won three straight. He scored on the power play and added an assist against Columbus on Tuesday, his second two-point game this month. Five goals in 20 games, playing 13:40 a night, is about what the Islanders could have asked.

The finishing is ahead of the chances: five goals on 2.8 expected goals (the quality of his shots), shooting 20.8% against a talent range around 14.5%. Speed and shot are still his gifts, with NHL Edge putting his top shot in the 94th percentile and his top speed in the 84th. The concern is the other way. The Islanders get 45% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, six and a half points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on the ice last season than with almost any forward. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows what he's for: 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net.
